newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dhaka stocks close sharply down on heavy selling.
newsitem.headline: Dhaka stocks close sharply down on heavy selling.

text.p: Dhaka stocks closed sharply down on heavy selling by small investors wary about the lingering bear run and future of the market, brokers said.
The market was nervous as hundreds of investors in the kerb market demonstrated outside the bourse protesting the persistent fall in share prices.

The Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) all-share price index fell 60.32 points or 6.28 at 899.38 on a turnover of 33.6 million taka. Losers led gainers by 105 to seven. Bangladesh Lamps lost 388 to 3,653, Amam Sea Food Industries shed 250 to 2,390 and Shine Pukur Holdings dropped 9.22 to 98.83.
DSE officials said the DSE authorities called police after angry protestors tried to lock the entrance of the bourse.

Broker Mahbub Morshed said the market was in crisis especially after commercial banks refused advances against shares to the investors. "The banks are reluctant to lend money when the market is falling every day," he said.
Brokers said the commercial banks were not providing loans to investors despite directives from the central bank. "We cannot gamble with public money," said one official with a commercial bank.
Broker Moshtaque Ahmed said: "The share prices dipped because the investors were wary about the prospect of the economy under present circumstances."
He, however, described the present share prices as attractive, and said: "I am buying shares every day in aniticipation of the better future of the market, especially after the next budget in June."
